full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-petitioners' case, in short, is that the land under the plaint schedule comprising an area of 1.10 acres being khas land admittediy belonged to Bangladesh Government and the plaintiffs are stranded persons from India and being the landless persons settled in the suit land 46 years before with permission from the then government authority. They removed jungle from the said land and converted it into cultivable and homestead land and started to live there. Later by permanent Settlement Case No.174 of 91-92, Bangladesh Government permanently entitled settlement of the plaintiff-respondent petitioners in the same land through a registered Kabuliyat dated 22-8-1991. The plaintiff petitioners mutated the suit land and also paid the rent as usual to the Government. At the instance of present high price of the land in the area due to establishment of India-Bangladesh Export-Import Station nearby the government officials being instigated by interested quarters without acknowledging the plaintiff-petitioners cancelled the permanent lease settlement on 26-4-2001 under the signature of defendant No.4 without serving any prior notice to the plaintiff petitioners and trying to make lease of the said land to third parties collusively. Consequently the plaintiff-petitioners are not bound by the illegal cancellation of the lease deed. Admittedly, there are dwelling houses of the plaintiff-petitioners over the suit land and in spite of that the defendant-opposite parties are trying to lease out the suit land to the third parties and hence the case. 

 4. The learned Advocate for the contesting defendants argued that admittedly the suit land belonged to Bangladesh Government and Government announced the suit land with other land as reserve forest by gazette notification and therefore, lease settlement of the suit land in the name of any person is not possible and thus by a resolution the Upazilla Land Settlement Committee cancelled the previous settlement. The suit land is not khas land and therefore, the lease settlement was void ab-initio and had no legal effect.
